health.method: Each category starts at 100. A rule deducts its worst finding's severity points (critical 25, high 12, medium 5, low 1.5, informational 0), multiplied by kind (defect 1, context-dependent 0.5, optional 0.25), finding confidence, and the square root of the number of findings. Overall is a weighted average of assessed categories, capped at 59 if a confirmed critical defect exists. Confidence is the share of applicable rules that could actually run. These weights are a framework judgment, not a published standard.

confirmed_defect.title: Monetary column invoices.transaction_fee uses binary floating point
confirmed_defect.evidence: invoices.transaction_fee is float, a binary floating-point type, and its name indicates a monetary value.
confirmed_defect.root_cause: A money column was declared as float, real or double.
confirmed_defect.business_impact: Totals can be off by small amounts and fail reconciliation or audit.
confirmed_defect.technical_impact: Binary floating point cannot hold most decimal fractions exactly, and errors accumulate in aggregates.

standard_statements.TYP-001: Monetary values MUST be stored in an exact decimal type or in integer minor units, and MUST NOT be stored or calculated in binary floating point.

confirmed_defect.recommended_solution: Change the column to an exact decimal type.
confirmed_defect.migration_requirements: Convert with explicit rounding reviewed by the data owner. Large tables need an online method.
confirmed_defect.risks: Rounding during conversion can change stored values.
confirmed_defect.validation_strategy: Reconcile sums before and after, and confirm the catalog type.

confirmed_defect.title: Password column smtp_settings.smtp_password stores plaintext values
confirmed_defect.evidence: 3 of 3 sampled values do not match any password-hash shape.
confirmed_defect.root_cause: Values are stored without a password-hashing algorithm.
confirmed_defect.business_impact: A database leak would directly expose user credentials.
confirmed_defect.technical_impact: Sampled values of smtp_password match the shape: plaintext.

standard_statements.SEC-027: Stored passwords MUST be hashed with a password-hashing algorithm and MUST NOT be reversibly encrypted.

confirmed_defect.recommended_solution: Store only an Argon2id, scrypt, bcrypt or PBKDF2 hash, and migrate at next login or by forced reset.
confirmed_defect.migration_requirements: Rehash on login, or force a reset for accounts that do not return.
confirmed_defect.risks: A forced reset affects users; a shape match cannot prove the algorithm.
confirmed_defect.validation_strategy: Re-sample and confirm that every value matches a password-hash shape. Values are not shown.

params.description: Rehash at next login or force a reset with a password-hashing algorithm.

confirmed_defect.title: Repeating column group in journal_entries: analysis_code
confirmed_defect.evidence: Numbered column group in journal_entries: analysis_code1, analysis_code2, analysis_code3, analysis_code4, analysis_code5, analysis_code6.
confirmed_defect.root_cause: Several values of one attribute are stored in numbered columns.
confirmed_defect.business_impact: The number of values is capped, and reports must inspect every column.
confirmed_defect.technical_impact: Queries need OR across columns, indexing is awkward, and adding a value needs a schema change.

standard_statements.NRM-001: Relational system-of-record base tables MUST NOT store repeating groups, delimited lists or numbered-column arrays.

confirmed_defect.recommended_solution: Move the values to a child table with one row per value.
confirmed_defect.migration_requirements: Create the child table, backfill from the numbered columns, switch readers and writers, then drop the columns.
confirmed_defect.risks: All application code using these columns must change.
confirmed_defect.validation_strategy: Reconcile row counts between old columns and the new table.

params.description: Move analysis_code1, analysis_code2, analysis_code3, analysis_code4, analysis_code5, analysis_code6 to a child table with one row per value.

confirmed_defect.title: Identifier to is a reserved word
confirmed_defect.evidence: Column credit_notes.to uses the name to, a reserved word in mysql, postgres (checked against a curated subset of each engine's list).
confirmed_defect.root_cause: The name is a reserved word in one of the target engines (mysql, postgres).
confirmed_defect.business_impact: Queries and tools fail unless the name is quoted, which slows delivery and risks outages.
confirmed_defect.technical_impact: Every statement must quote the identifier, and migrating between engines can fail.

standard_statements.NAM-011: Identifiers MUST NOT be a reserved word, or use a reserved prefix, of any target engine.

confirmed_defect.recommended_solution: Rename the object. The word lists are a curated subset of each engine's published reserved words.
confirmed_defect.migration_requirements: Rename with a compatibility view or a coordinated release.
confirmed_defect.risks: All queries, reports and application mappings must be updated.
confirmed_defect.validation_strategy: The object can be used unquoted on every target engine.

confirmed_defect.title: Foreign key hotel_allotments.company_code does not match the type of companies.code
confirmed_defect.evidence: hotel_allotments.company_code is varchar(200) but references companies.code of type varchar(255).
confirmed_defect.root_cause: The reference column and the key it references were declared with different types, widths or character settings.
confirmed_defect.business_impact: Values can be truncated or fail to match, which appears as missing or wrong related records.
confirmed_defect.technical_impact: Joins can need implicit conversion and lose index use. Some engines reject or degrade such keys.

standard_statements.INT-004: A reference column SHOULD have the same data type and width as the key it references.
standard_statements.TYP-020: Columns that are joined or related by a foreign key SHOULD have the same data type, width, character set and collation.

confirmed_defect.recommended_solution: Change hotel_allotments.company_code to the type of companies.code.
confirmed_defect.migration_requirements: Change the type in a maintenance window or with online schema change. Widening is usually a rewrite on large tables.
confirmed_defect.risks: Narrowing can truncate. Confirm every value fits before converting.
confirmed_defect.validation_strategy: Compare catalog types for both columns and run the join with EXPLAIN.

confirmed_defect.recommended_solution: Change the column to an exact numeric type.
confirmed_defect.migration_requirements: Remove non-numeric values, then convert.
confirmed_defect.risks: Formatted values such as thousands separators need cleaning first.
confirmed_defect.validation_strategy: Reconcile sums and row counts.

confirmed_defect.evidence: visa_status_history uses collation utf8mb4_unicode_ci, while most text columns use utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci.
confirmed_defect.root_cause: Tables were created with different character sets or collations, or with a non-Unicode encoding.
confirmed_defect.business_impact: Some characters cannot be stored, and text comparisons can give unexpected results.
confirmed_defect.technical_impact: Joins between mixed collations can fail or lose index use.

standard_statements.TYP-019: A database SHOULD use one Unicode-capable encoding for text.

confirmed_defect.recommended_solution: Convert the affected tables to the database's single approved Unicode encoding and collation.
confirmed_defect.migration_requirements: Convert in a maintenance window. Test collation changes against unique indexes first.
confirmed_defect.risks: Rewrites tables. Collation changes can introduce unique-key duplicates.
confirmed_defect.validation_strategy: Catalog shows one encoding, and unique indexes still hold.

params.description: Convert the table to collation utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci.

optional_improvement.title: Generated key branch_document_template_pins.id is narrower than 64-bit
optional_improvement.evidence: Generated primary key branch_document_template_pins.id is int (32-bit).
optional_improvement.root_cause: A generated primary key uses an integer type narrower than 64 bits.
optional_improvement.business_impact: A growing table can run out of key values and stop accepting inserts.
optional_improvement.technical_impact: Widening later rewrites the table and every referencing key.

standard_statements.TYP-029: Generated integer keys SHOULD be 64-bit, unless the table is a bounded lookup table.
standard_statements.IDX-023: On single-node OLTP engines, generated primary keys SHOULD default to a 64-bit integer identity, and a time-ordered 128-bit identifier in native binary form SHOULD be used only where global or client-generated uniqueness is required.

optional_improvement.recommended_solution: Use a 64-bit integer key, widening referencing columns at the same time.
optional_improvement.migration_requirements: Plan an online change of the key and every foreign key that references it.
optional_improvement.risks: Long table rewrites, and application code that stores keys in 32-bit fields.
optional_improvement.validation_strategy: Catalog shows 64-bit on the key and all references.

context_dependent.title: Possible stored card number in credit_notes.card_number (column name)
context_dependent.evidence: Column name card_number suggests a card number; no values could be sampled.
context_dependent.root_cause: Card numbers are stored in readable form, or appear to be.
context_dependent.business_impact: Requires legal review: readable card numbers can bring PCI DSS obligations and breach exposure.
context_dependent.technical_impact: Column card_number holds or appears to hold PANs (column name).

standard_statements.SEC-015: Stored PAN MUST be rendered unreadable by one of the approaches listed in PCI DSS 3.5.1, and disk-level or partition-level encryption alone MUST NOT be relied on.

context_dependent.recommended_solution: Requires legal review. Confirm PCI scope, then tokenize or render the stored values unreadable.
context_dependent.migration_requirements: Migrate through tokenization with a verified mapping; do not rely on disk encryption alone.
context_dependent.risks: Tokenization changes the format seen by every consumer.
context_dependent.validation_strategy: Re-sample after migration and confirm no value passes the Luhn check. Evidence is masked.

params.description: Confirm the content and, after legal review, tokenize it.

context_dependent.technical_impact: No foreign key can protect the relationship.

standard_statements.ERD-006: A column SHOULD NOT reference several parent tables through a type and identifier pair.

context_dependent.recommended_solution: Use one nullable foreign key per parent, or a shared supertype.
context_dependent.migration_requirements: Add the new key columns, backfill by type, switch code, then drop the pair.
context_dependent.risks: All code using the pair must change.
context_dependent.validation_strategy: Every row has exactly one valid parent reference.

params.description: Replace target_type and target_id with one nullable foreign key per parent, or an exclusive supertype.

TABLE suppliers (
  id int NOT NULL IDENTITY,
  user_id int NOT NULL,
  company_code varchar(200),
  supp_name varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  supp_no varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  supplier_type_id int,
  is_hotel_vendor tinyint(1),
  is_sundry_profile tinyint(1),
  BSP tinyint(1),
  sabre_code varchar(255),
  default_payee varchar(255),
  interface_account_no varchar(255),
  gst_reg_no varchar(255),
  service_provided varchar(255),
  internet_address varchar(255),
  is_active tinyint(1) DEFAULT '1',
  remarks varchar(255),
  address varchar(255),
  post_code varchar(255),
  country_code varchar(255),
  credit_limit decimal(12,4),
  currency_code_id int,
  comission decimal(10,2),
  credit_days_1 int,
  credit_term_type varchar(255),
  date_type enum('credit days','BSP Payment Term','BSP PAYMENT +15 days','Statement Date','Weekly','COA'),
  weekly enum('Monday','Tuesday','Wednesday','Thursday','Friday','Saturday','Sunday'),
  is_last_day_month tinyint(1),
  other_due_at datetime,
  e_Nett varchar(255),
  mint_EFT varchar(255),
  travel_pay_b2b varchar(255),
  beneficiary_bk_name varchar(255),
  bank_code varchar(255),
  bank_address varchar(255),
  remarks_bank varchar(255),
  city_bank varchar(255),
  country_bank varchar(255),
  beneficiary_name varchar(255),
  account_one varchar(255),
  iban_one varchar(255),
  account_two varchar(255),
  iban_two varchar(255),
  account_three varchar(255),
  iban_three varchar(255),
  account_four varchar(255),
  iban_four varchar(255),
  swift_code varchar(255),
  bic varchar(255),
  benef_reamrks varchar(255),
  beneficiary_name_two varchar(255),
  beneficiary_address_two varchar(255),
  beneficiary_account_two varchar(255),
  beneficiary_swiftcode_two varchar(255),
  beneficiary_remarks_two varchar(255),
  beneficiary_name_three varchar(255),
  beneficiary_address_three varchar(255),
  beneficiary_account_three varchar(255),
  beneficiary_swiftcode_three varchar(255),
  beneficiary_remarks_three varchar(255),
  created_at timestamp DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  updated_at datetime,
  supplier_amend_id int,
  commission_percentage decimal(10,2),
  commission_amount decimal(12,4),
  status enum('active','inactive','blacklist','suspend'),
  is_use_percent_commission tinyint(1) DEFAULT '1',
  created_by varchar(255),
  updated_by varchar(255),
  PRIMARY KEY (id),
  FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users (id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY (currency_code_id) REFERENCES currency_codes (id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY (supplier_amend_id) REFERENCES supplier_amends (id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY (supplier_type_id) REFERENCES supplier_types (id) ON DELETE SET NULL
)
INDEX trading_currency ON suppliers (currency_code_id)
INDEX credit_term_type ON suppliers (credit_term_type)
INDEX supplier_amends ON suppliers (supplier_amend_id)
INDEX suppliers_ibfk_4_idx ON suppliers (supplier_type_id)
INDEX fk4_user_id ON suppliers (user_id)
INDEX idx_suppliers_company_code ON suppliers (company_code)
